plan.title: Context-Aware Task Execution with Smart Subagent Spawning
plan.overview: Transform festina-implement from inline task execution to a subagent orchestration model. Each plan task spawns a fresh general-purpose subagent with explicit file references to read, ensuring clean context. The orchestrator persists task completion after each subagent finishes and runs quality verification only after all tasks complete. This follows the orchestrator pattern (thin orchestrator, delegates to subagents) already established in festina-scope.

approach.rationale:
Following two existing patterns: - Subagent spawning: Task tool with subagent_type in festina-scope at apps/festinalente/src/content/skills/festina-scope/SKILL.md:222-328 - Orchestrator pattern: Thin coordination layer that delegates work, documented at .festinalente/engineering/patterns/orchestrator.md
Key design decisions from scoping: 1. All tasks use subagents (no complexity threshold) — ensures fresh context for every task 2. File references only in prompts (no embedded code) — keeps prompts lean 3. Sequential execution — respects task dependencies via depends attribute 4. Quality checks (TODO scan, requirement trace, wiring) stay in orchestrator — run once after all tasks 5. Directive loading stays in orchestrator — not passed to subagents
Trade-off: Slightly higher latency per task (subagent spawn overhead) in exchange for unlimited plan size and guaranteed fresh context.

change.new: Task element adds: context element with file children
change.affects: plan.xml template, festina-plan skill, plan handler (if exists)

task.name: Add context element to plan.xml template
task.pattern: Existing task element structure in template
task.action:
- Add `context` element inside task element after pattern - Context contains `file` children with path attribute - Include comments explaining what goes in context: - Existing files that need to be read before implementation - Pattern reference files - Files that contain imports/types needed
Current structure (approximate): ```xml <task id="1" type="auto"> <name>...</name> <files>...</files> <requirements>...</requirements> <pattern>...</pattern> <action>...</action> <verify>...</verify> <done>...</done> </task> ```
Change to: ```xml <task id="1" type="auto"> <name>...</name> <files>...</files> <requirements>...</requirements> <pattern>...</pattern> <context> <file>path/to/existing/file.ts</file> <file>path/to/pattern/reference.ts</file> </context> <action>...</action> <verify>...</verify> <done>...</done> </task> ```
task.done: Template has context element with file children inside task element

pitfalls.pitfall: Task prompt must be complete enough for single-agent execution
Only include file paths, never embed content — subagent reads fresh
Always include spec file path so subagent can read full requirements
Must write plan.xml after each task completes to survive context exhaustion
